newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian TV crew seized in Chechnya, no demands yet.
newsitem.headline: Russian TV crew seized in Chechnya, no demands yet.

text.p: Armed gunmen seized a Russian television crew in the breakaway region of Chechnya, officials from NTV commercial television said on Sunday.
One official said the crew -- two men and a women -- were seized on Saturday afternoon near the village of Samashki, some 30 km west of the regional capital Grozny.
They had been filming a rally in central Grozny and were returning to base with their pictures, she said.
The kidnappers had not made any demands and NTV's efforts to contact the Chechen leadership to ask for help had not been successful so far.
Chechnya, which fought a 21-month war with Russian troops sent in to crush its independence bid, has become a difficult place for journalists to work and hostage takings are common.
One group of reporters has already been held for more than three months, although other groups have been held and freed.
Ekho Moskvy radio station quoted Chechen First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov as saying Chechen forces had spent all night looking for the kidnappers.

"The Chechen leadership takes full responsibility for events taking place on the territory of Chechnya and views the kidnapping of journalists as another mean and insidious challenge," he said. "The response will be tough and cruel."
